A California Apple user has filed a class action lawsuit accusing the company of misleading consumers about its "Hide My Email" privacy feature. The details are as follows.

Apple Sued Over Hide My Email Vulnerability

A few days ago, 404 Media reported that Apple had known about a so-called vulnerability for over a year, which could potentially leak the real email address behind a Hide My Email alias.

Apple's Hide My Email feature allows users to create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their personal inboxes, enabling users to sign up for apps, websites, and newsletters without revealing their real addresses.

The feature is offered for free through "Sign in with Apple"; the iCloud+ plan (starting at $0.99 per month) includes a more comprehensive version, allowing users to create aliases for websites, newsletters, and other services.

According to 404 Media, a security researcher notified Apple of the vulnerability in June 2025, warning that it could expose the real email addresses behind Hide My Email aliases.

Apple reportedly acknowledged receiving the report about a month later, but allegedly failed to address the issue. In March 2026, the company stated it had fixed the vulnerability, but the researcher discovered it remained exploitable.

Returning to the lawsuit itself (reported by MacRumors), plaintiff Anthony Alvarez stated:

Apple knew of the issue over a year ago, and the vulnerability remains unfixed to this day—meanwhile, Apple continues to profit from Hide My Email and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of paying iCloud+ subscribers who relied on Apple's claims, trusting that Hide My Email would protect their personal email addresses from being exposed. The plaintiff and class members paid Apple for privacy protection—iCloud+ subscribers through the premium included in their iCloud+ subscription fees, and all Apple customers through the premium built into Apple products, which Apple markets as offering enhanced privacy protections and features such as Hide My Email.

The lawsuit also claims this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report indicating that Apple's randomized MAC address feature might expose users' real hardware identifiers.

The complaint further alleges that the proposed class members' total claims exceed $5 million (excluding interest and legal fees), though it does not explain how that figure was calculated.

Alvarez filed the lawsuit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers he claims have been similarly affected. He is asking the court to certify the case as a class action, covering four proposed user groups:

  • A nationwide group of Apple customers who purchased devices and used Hide My Email;
  • A California subgroup of the above users;
  • A nationwide subgroup of iCloud+ subscribers who used the feature;
  • A California subgroup of iCloud+ subscribers.

He has requested a jury trial and is seeking unspecified monetary damages, as well as a court order requiring Apple to either fix Hide My Email or clearly disclose its limitations.

Apple has not yet responded to the lawsuit.
